headline: Markets slip on geopolitical tensions and defense sector concerns
deck: Broad equity declines amid escalating Middle East conflict and military spending implications.
body:
U.S. equities edged lower across all three major indices today, with the Dow leading losses at -0.69% while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq held relatively steady at -0.24% and -0.25% respectively. The modest selloff reflects investor caution as geopolitical risks intensify, particularly surrounding Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the Houthis in the Middle East. Bond yields ticked down slightly, with the 10-year Treasury falling 4 basis points to 5.27%, suggesting a flight to safety among fixed-income investors.

Geopolitical flashpoints dominated today's headlines, from escalating Saudi-Houthi conflicts causing flight disruptions in Riyadh to renewed hypersonic missile threats from Russia and China. A former defense secretary's comments on the Iran situation, combined with satellite and defense sector commentary on emerging space threats, point to prolonged elevated defense spending and potential supply chain disruptions. These tensions typically support defense contractors but can create broader market uncertainty if they threaten global trade routes or energy supplies.

On the corporate side, the finalized Skydance-WBD acquisition and Ryanair's warning about sustained high jet fuel costs into 2028 highlight mixed sectoral pressures. Media consolidation and aviation sector margin compression offset any enthusiasm from M&A activity, keeping sentiment cautious as investors weigh near-term earnings headwinds against longer-term growth opportunities.
